strengths: Addresses a relevant question: which latent factors multimodal contrastive learning can recover when modalities have distinct, noisy generative processes.
The proposed FastICA postprocessing is simple and applicable to frozen CLIP encoders. Experiments cover synthetic recovery, CelebA traversals, multiple backbones, and several few-shot settings.
Reports promising empirical results, including high synthetic recovery scores and an improvement in ViT-B/16 two-shot target-domain average accuracy from 32.51 to 37.13 with PCA and ICA.
weaknesses: The central identifiability proofs contain a fundamental error. Appendices A.4.1 and A.5.1 assert that optimal encoders must produce identical embeddings for every positive pair (Eqs. 27 and 49). Under the stipulated noisy conditionals with full support, this forces constant embeddings, contradicting the claimed uniformity and recovery. Alignment and uniformity cannot be minimized independently as asserted. Consequently, the subsequent removal of modality-specific variables and identifiability conclusions lack valid proofs.

The convex-body proof additionally assumes an exactly uniform marginal p(z_t), although Lemma 4.2 establishes only a limit as lambda approaches zero. For finite lambda, boundary-dependent normalization generally makes this marginal nonuniform, even on an interval with a truncated Laplace conditional. The substitution leading to Eq. 56 and the claimed symmetric cross-entropy reduction therefore do not follow. No approximation bound addresses this discrepancy.

The theoretical justification for ICA is insufficient. Under the assumed uniform spherical distribution, coordinates are dependent and all orthogonal rotations have the same distribution. FastICA therefore cannot select the ground-truth axes under these assumptions. Section 4's local-isometry and PCA discussion does not establish that pretrained CLIP satisfies the alternative convex-body assumptions.

The downstream experiments do not isolate ICA's contribution. Appendix A.8 uses 300 components for ICA and 160 or 200 for PCA plus ICA, without dimension-matched PCA-only or whitening-only controls. For fixed whitening and retained dimensions, an orthogonal ICA rotation leaves the optimum of the stated L2-regularized linear probe unchanged. The reported gains could consequently reflect dimensionality reduction and whitening rather than disentanglement.

The CelebA disentanglement evidence relies on selected traversals and subjective attribute counts. Comparing 16 identified attributes against previously reported counts of 8 and 15 is not a controlled comparison. Quantitative disentanglement measurements, a reproducible attribute-selection protocol, and matched baselines are missing; some showcased directions explicitly combine attributes, such as gender and mustache.

Evaluation reliability and reproducibility are insufficient. Real-data tables omit uncertainty across support-set draws, and the data used to fit PCA and ICA are unclear. Appendix A.8 states that regularization is selected on each dataset's validation split, leaving possible target-label use unresolved for domain generalization. Table 3 also reports the RN101 baseline target average as 20.03, although its listed values average 22.03.
